findings.title: coins-view-cache-wipe keeps the coins DB best-block pointer, so a crashed -reindex-chainstate restarts at the old tip over an empty UTXO set
findings.core_does: -reindex-chainstate opens the coins DB with should_wipe=options.wipe_chainstate_db (node/chainstate.cpp:93), a full LevelDB wipe that removes DB_BEST_BLOCK with everything else, and is_coinsview_empty() is `wipe_chainstate_db || CoinsTip().GetBestBlock().IsNull()` (node/chainstate.cpp:69-70), so LoadChainTip is SKIPPED and the chain stays at genesis until the replay rebuilds it. Core cannot reach a state where the coins DB is empty and its best-block key still names an old tip: the key lives in the same LevelDB that was wiped, and CCoinsViewDB::BatchWrite erases and rewrites it inside the coin batch (txdb.cpp:128,159).
findings.we_do: bl.store:coins-view-db-erase-all-coins deliberately erases only 'C'-prefixed coin keys and leaves every non-coin key intact, so the 'B' best-block pointer survives the wipe; coins-view-cache-wipe (src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:324) also leaves the cache's own cvc-best-block set. do-reindex-chainstate (src/node/reindex.lisp:55-60) rewinds chainstate.dat to genesis with the in-transition marker and then wipes. If the process dies before the first replay flush, startup runs recover-inconsistent-chainstate's genesis branch (src/node/recovery.lisp:132-146), which re-wipes and clears the marker -- and then %init-services runs reconcile-coins-db-best-block UNCONDITIONALLY (src/node/init.lisp:864), sees the surviving pointer naming the pre-wipe tip, finds that block in the index, and moves chainstate.dat FORWARD to it, logging 'Recovered'.
findings.impact: The node comes up claiming the pre-reindex tip height with a completely EMPTY UTXO set, and reports it as a successful recovery. gettxoutsetinfo/scantxoutset answer for an empty set at that height. The next real block that spends anything fails validate-block with :missing-input, which is on *deterministic-invalid-block-errors* (src/validation/block.lisp:3134-3141), so %mark-block-subtree-invalid poisons that block and its whole descendant subtree :invalid and persists it -- the node permanently marks the honest chain invalid and will not follow it again without a manual wipe. Core's equivalent path leaves the chain at genesis and replays.
findings.executed: Probe on the warm image (regtest, LevelDB-backed coins-view-cache): mined 5 blocks, flushed (pointer = tip 9cf8989a..., height 5), then reproduced the crash state (update-chain-tip to genesis + save-state :in-transition t + coins-view-cache-wipe). The pointer after the wipe was still 9cf8989a... . load-state returned :INCONSISTENT; recover-inconsistent-chainstate returned T leaving height 0 and total amount 0; reconcile-coins-db-best-block then returned :RECONCILED and left FINAL-HEIGHT 5, FINAL-TIP-IS-OLD-TIP T, FINAL-UTXO-AMOUNT 0, FINAL-UTXO-COUNT 0.

findings.title: A snapshot chainstate's header-index delta is bound to a stale snapshot CRC, so the whole delta is discarded at the next start
findings.core_does: The block index and everything that persists it live in BlockManager (m_blockman), OUTSIDE any chainstate: one m_block_index map, one m_dirty_blockindex set, one WriteBlockIndexDB. Adding a snapshot chainstate adds no second copy of that persistence state, so there is nothing per-chainstate that can go stale relative to the on-disk index.
findings.we_do: %make-snapshot-chainstate shares :block-index with the primary but the two crc/counter slots that bind the header-index DELTA log to its snapshot (chain-state-header-index-snapshot-crc / -delta-entries, src/storage/chain.lisp:46-48) are PER chain-state struct and are not copied -- the snapshot chainstate starts with crc NIL. %flush-chainstate calls save-header-index on EVERY chainstate (src/node/flush.lisp:250-251, driven by maybe-periodic-flush's 'flush every chainstate' loop at :386-389). A NIL crc sends save-header-index down the %write-header-index-snapshot branch, which rewrites the whole shared index, DELETES the delta and adopts the new crc for that chainstate only -- leaving the other chainstate's crc pointing at a snapshot that no longer exists. Whichever chainstate next CREATES the delta file writes ITS crc into the log header (src/storage/chain.lisp:1084-1090), and if that is the stale one, %replay-header-index-delta refuses the log at startup and deletes it (src/storage/chain.lisp:1197-1204).
findings.impact: With an assumeutxo snapshot chainstate in use, every block-index change since the last full snapshot -- statuses (:valid / :invalid), tx-count, nFile/nDataPos/nUndoPos -- is silently dropped on the next unclean start, which is exactly the failure %entry-persist-key's and %delta-entry-width's own docstrings say the design exists to prevent ('a missed status mark means a block marked :invalid quietly reverts to :valid on the next restart'). An operator invalidateblock is reverted; recently connected blocks come back as header-only; recorded undo positions are lost so the next disconnect/reconnect appends duplicate undo records. Nothing is logged. A CLEAN shutdown is unaffected (it force-fulls every chainstate).
findings.executed: Probe on the warm image: cs1 (primary) wrote the full snapshot (crc b28c37cf); cs2 built exactly as %make-snapshot-chainstate builds it (same base-path, :block-index shared) reported crc NIL. e1 changed -> cs1 appended a delta (log present). e2 changed -> cs2's save-header-index wrote a FULL snapshot, deleted the delta and took crc 54642735, while cs1's crc stayed b28c37cf. e3 was then marked :invalid and persisted through cs1 (delta present again). After a reload: e1 :VALID, e2 :VALID, e3 :HEADER-VALID -- expected (:VALID :VALID :INVALID). The :invalid mark was lost.

findings.title: Header-index delta replay leaves two objects per refreshed block, and the active-chain walk hands out the orphan
findings.core_does: LoadBlockIndexGuts materialises every CBlockIndex through BlockManager::InsertBlockIndex, a try_emplace on m_block_index, and resolves each pprev through the SAME function -- so there is exactly one CBlockIndex object per hash and a pprev pointer and a m_block_index lookup can never disagree.
findings.we_do: %replay-header-index-delta parses each delta record into a BRAND-NEW block-index-entry and (setf (gethash hash index) e), then relinks only the entries the delta itself carried ((link-header-entries index prev-all), src/storage/chain.lisp:1240-1242). Any entry that was in the snapshot and did NOT change keeps its prev-entry pointing at the SUPERSEDED object for its parent. Since the load is by hash but every ancestry walk (collect-chain-entries, find-fork-point, entry-ancestor-at-height, %activation-step-target) follows prev-entry, the two views of the same block then differ on every MUTABLE field: status, tx-count, file/data-pos/undo-pos. %reorg-disconnect (src/validation/block.lisp:3424) and %reorg-connect (:3532) set status on entries obtained from exactly such a walk, and save-header-index only ever iterates the hash table, so those writes are invisible to the persisted index. block-descends-from-p's docstring (src/validation/block.lisp:3838-3853) explicitly asserts the opposite ('load-header-index rebuilds a consistent object graph by hash').
findings.impact: After any restart that replays a delta, the in-memory block index holds two contradictory copies of every entry the delta refreshed, and reorg-phase status updates for those blocks are silently dropped from headerindex.dat. Reachable without assumeutxo: pruning clears an old entry's file/data-pos while its already-connected child does not change, and getblock/gettxoutproof lazily backfill tx-count (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:1573,1580) on old entries the same way. The stale copy also keeps claiming a data-pos for a block whose body has been pruned.
findings.executed: Probe on the warm image. (a) Two-entry case: snapshot A(:header-valid, no data-pos) and its child B; then A -> :invalid + data-pos 4242; delta; reload. index[A] read :INVALID/4242 while B's prev-entry read :HEADER-VALID/NIL and was not EQ to index[A]. (b) Active-chain case: G-A-B-C all :valid with positions, snapshot, then A pruned (file/data-pos cleared), delta, reload. collect-chain-entries from the tip returned heights (3 2 1) and the height-1 entry was NOT EQ to (get-block-index-entry cs 1); it still reported data-pos 100 while the live entry reported NIL. Applying %reorg-disconnect's own (setf status :header-valid) over the walked list left the live entry at :VALID, and %changed-header-index-entries then saw 2 changed entries instead of 3.

findings.title: VerifyDB never runs at startup and verifychain implements only Core's levels 0-1
findings.core_does: LoadChainstate runs CVerifyDB().VerifyDB() over EVERY non-empty chainstate on every boot with -checkblocks (default 6) and -checklevel (default 3): level 1 re-reads and CheckBlock's each of the last N blocks, level 2 reads and verifies their undo records, level 3 DisconnectBlock's them against the coins cache and level 4 reconnects them. CORRUPTED_BLOCK_DB is a hard startup failure ('Corrupted block database detected').
findings.we_do: Nothing calls verifychain, or anything like it, from start-node; -checkblocks and -checklevel are on the accept-and-drop list (src/config-options.lisp:438). The verifychain RPC itself stops at Core's level 1: it re-reads each of the last nblocks blocks and re-checks the merkle root and proof of work, and never touches the undo records or the coins view, so Core's levels 2-4 -- the ones that compare the block database against the UTXO set -- do not exist anywhere in the tree.
findings.impact: A chainstate that disagrees with its blocks is never detected. That is what turns the bbf6e679 corruption above from 'refuses to start' into 'runs and reports success': Core's level-3 pass disconnects the last 6 blocks against the coins cache and would fail on an empty UTXO set at height N immediately. It also means torn undo records, a rev file lost with its blk file, and a coins DB restored from a mismatched backup all go unreported until a reorg or a spend hits them.
findings.executed: Read-only: grepped the whole tree for checkblocks/checklevel/verifychain/VerifyDB; the only hits are the option table (accept-and-drop), the RPC and its test. No startup call site exists. Named as an uncovered Core subsystem in docs/gap-analysis-10-critic.md line 30 but never filed as a finding, and absent from exclusions.md.

findings.title: Every periodic flush empties the whole coins cache; Core only Syncs on the time and count triggers
findings.core_does: FlushStateToDisk computes empty_cache = (mode == FORCE_FLUSH) || fCacheLarge || fCacheCritical and then does `empty_cache ? CoinsTip().Flush() : CoinsTip().Sync()` (validation.cpp:2812). A write driven only by fPeriodicWrite -- the DATABASE_WRITE_INTERVAL timer, the analogue of our 600 s / 25 000-block triggers -- takes the Sync branch: dirty coins are committed and the entries STAY in the cache.
findings.we_do: %flush-chainstate Phase 2 unconditionally calls coins-view-cache-flush, which commits the batch and then CLRHASHes the whole table and zeroes mem-bytes (src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:453-486). We already have the exact Sync counterpart (coins-view-cache-sync, :381) and use it for the RPC walk sites, but the flush never chooses between them; the trigger that fired is not passed down to Phase 2. maybe-periodic-flush also flushes every OTHER chainstate once any trigger fires (src/node/flush.lisp:386-389), so a clean chainstate has its warm cache dropped too.
findings.impact: On a node following the tip the 600 s timer fires continuously, so up to the whole -dbcache (450 MiB by default) of warm UTXO entries is discarded every ten minutes and has to be re-read from LevelDB. That is the cost the *coins-cache-budget-bytes* docstring itself identifies as the dominant IBD cost ('profiled I/O-wait-bound at mainnet h~828k'). Correctness is unaffected -- a cleared cache is refilled by pull-through reads.
findings.executed: Read-only: traced the three triggers in maybe-periodic-flush (src/node/flush.lisp:369-379) and maybe-critical-flush against Core's empty_cache expression; only the size trigger corresponds to Core's fCacheLarge/fCacheCritical. Not measured on the image.

coverage_note: COVERED, with execution on the project container (regtest fixtures + a LevelDB-backed coins-view-cache, four probes): the crash matrix around %flush-chainstate's three phases; recover-inconsistent-chainstate and reconcile-coins-db-best-block composed in the order %init-load-chain -> %init-recover-chain -> %init-services actually runs them; do-reindex-chainstate's wipe/replay and its two existing crash tests; the header-index snapshot + delta log (binding CRC, truncated frame, entry-width versioning, object graph after replay); coins-view-cache sync vs flush and the FRESH/DIRTY post-conditions; perform-reorg's five pre-mutation refusals (pruned fork point, :invalid branch, witness-stripped self-heal, missing bodies, corrupt undo) and the phase A/B/C status writes; prune-old-blocks / prune-blocks-to-height / prune-flat-block-file / prune-lock-ceiling against FindFilesToPrune and PRUNE_LOCK_BUFFER; the assumeutxo dual-chainstate cache rebalance, prune floor and shared block index; VerifyDB and ReplayBlocks against node/chainstate.cpp. VERIFIED-CORRECT, no finding filed: the truncated-frame stop in %replay-header-index-delta (a short or CRC-failing frame stops replay and keeps every complete frame; a zero count and an over-long frame both terminate); the delta-version gate that replays a v1 log at its own 185-byte width instead of discarding it; blk/rev writes are fsynced per record, which is STRICTER than Core's FlushBlockFile; Phase 1 writes the header index BEFORE the coins batch, matching WriteBlockIndexDB-then-Sync; the coins DB pointer is staged in the SAME writebatch as the coins; %save-undo-flat's write-once guard; the reorg's undo-availability precheck (Core DISCONNECT_FAILED); +min-blocks-to-keep+ = 288 = MIN_BLOCKS_TO_KEEP and +prune-lock-buffer+ = 10 = PRUNE_LOCK_BUFFER. EXAMINED AND NOT FILED: %coinbase-committed-p's monotone-probe premise is false for a block whose coinbase output 0 is provably unspendable (script-unspendable-p outputs are dropped from the UTXO set, coins-view-cache.lisp:635), which makes the recovery walk rewind further than the truth -- but reconcile-coins-db-best-block runs afterwards and moves the record back to the exact pointer, so the consequence is a longer walk and a misleading log line, not a wrong tip; the same probe returns NIL for genesis, so any walk that reaches height 0 ends in 'no committed ancestor found on disk' and a refusal to start, and I could not construct a reachable path to that. NOT COVERED, and which GA11 dimension inherits it: the per-index best-block markers and their startup catch-up/rewind (base-index index-prepare-sync / index-sync, txindex, blockfilterindex, coinstatsindex, txospenderindex) belong to storage-indexes; assumeutxo snapshot LOADING and hash verification (loadtxoutset, the snapshot metadata format, promote/rename of chainstate_snapshot) belong to storage-indexes or a dedicated assumeutxo pass; the LevelDB wrapper itself (bl.kv: WAL, fsync, iterator lifetime, error surfaces) was treated as sound and belongs to the never-opened-files dimension; the flat block-file format's own reader/writer framing (magic, length prefix, %scan-flat-block-files enumeration) was read but not fuzzed, which the differential-harness lane inherits; the mempool.dat / fee-estimate / banlist persistence paths were out of scope; nothing here was run against a real testnet4 datadir, so no claim rests on production-scale timing.
